To: t-4471
Replying to: p01
Cc: none
Subject: Draft for review: Cascade Legal Rights Project response and Nov. 14 clinic update

We’re responding on behalf of Cascade Legal Rights Project because the concerns raised here deserve a clear answer. Receiving a letter from a landlord’s lawyer soon after asking for help can be frightening. We understand why people would have questions about whether their information was shared, and we appreciate the opportunity to explain our policy.

Our policy prohibits sharing, selling, or disclosing clinic attendees’ information to landlords or their attorneys. Clinic sign-in records are retained internally in locked storage. We will not discuss or confirm anyone’s attendance or individual circumstances on this board, including in response to the concerns raised here. Protecting people’s privacy matters more than debating a particular account in public.

Magistrate-court eviction filings are public records. Some law firms use those records to send mailings to tenants. Public filings are a likely explanation for the letters described here, but we cannot establish the source of any particular letter from this discussion. Receiving a mailing does not, by itself, mean that someone’s information came from the clinic.

The free tenant rights clinic is still happening Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. The library meeting room is closed that day for repairs, so the clinic has moved to Mt Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta. The accessible side entrance is by the parking lot. No appointment is needed. Volunteer attorneys and staff can review eviction notices and court papers and explain your options.

You are still welcome, including if you have questions or concerns about the clinic. Please contact clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. To protect your privacy, please do not post names, addresses, case details, or documents here. We welcome questions through those direct channels.
